newsitem.title: USA: Applied Materials shares surge after earnings.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials shares surge after earnings.

text.p: Shares of Applied Materials Inc. surged Wednesday after the semiconductor equipment maker reported earnings that were far better than Wall Street expected.

The biggest maker of manufacturing gear for computer chip factories also told investors that sales for its advanced equipment are picking up again, a sign that the entire capital equipment industry could be climbing out of a year-long trough, analysts said.

"It's a good sign for everybody, but there's a handful of companies that are doing better than others," said Mark FitzGerald, analyst at UBS Securities in San Francisco. "Applied Materials is one of them."
Shares of Applied Materials, based in Santa Clara, Calif., jumped $9.125 to $99.375 on Nasdaq trading of 12.4 million shares, making them among the most active.
Shares of other equipment makers rose also. Novellus Systems Inc. gained $4.50 to $111.875 and LAM Research Corp. rose $3.328 to $58.75.

After the market closed Tuesday, Applied Materials said it had fiscal third-quater profit before charges of $145.2 million, or 77 cents a share. Wall Street had expected earnings per share of 68 cents a share, according to First Call.
Applied Materials' executives also told investors that they expect strong orders in the fourth quarter as well, analysts who heard the call said.
The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of $1.22 billion and earnings per share of 90 cents, higher than what most analysts had predicted.
Applied Materials said big chip manufacturers are investing heavily in next-generation chipmaking equipment, even though prices of memory chips continue to slump.
Asian producers in particular are placing heavy orders for the new equipment, the company said.
